headline: HSC and equivalent exam results to be published on October 31, two days later than planned
summary: The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the revised date, initially set for October 29. Over 1.27 million candidates registered for this year's examinations.
details: The results of this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than initially scheduled for October 29.

The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the revised date in a notice issued yesterday. The notice was signed by committee president Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, also chairman of the Dhaka Education Board.
The results will be announced at 11:00 AM at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka and will be made available simultaneously at educational institutions and online.

Students can check their results through their respective education boards’ websites or via SMS. Applications for re-scrutiny will be accepted online from November 1 to 7, with details available on the education boards’ websites.
A total of 1,270,583 candidates registered for this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards.

headline_marked: [[LPG price hike likely]] as BERC schedules public hearing amid consumer overpayments
headline: LPG price hike likely as BERC schedules public hearing amid consumer overpayments
summary: Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) is set to hold a public hearing to review LPG prices, a move that could lead to another increase for consumers already paying significantly above official rates for over a month.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) is initiating a process to revise LPG rates and charges, with a public hearing scheduled for tomorrow. This comes after industry players requested an increase, hinting at a likely price hike for consumers.

Consumers have been paying well above BERC-fixed prices for over a month. For instance, a 12kg cylinder, officially priced at Tk 1,837 since October 4, is currently being sold for Tk 2,200 to Tk 2,400 in the retail market.

The discrepancy stems from various points in the supply chain. Distributors report paying more than Tk 1,850 per cylinder and charging retailers above the prescribed distribution charge, leading to retailers acquiring cylinders at least Tk 2,100 each.

Four distributors from Dhaka, Cumilla, Chattogram, and Gazipur applied to BERC on October 13, seeking to raise distribution charges from Tk 50 to Tk 150 and retail charges from Tk 45 to Tk 70 per cylinder, citing increased fuel costs and operational expenses.

LPG importers have also requested an increase in storage and bottling charges from Tk 16.74 to Tk 25 per kilogram. They attribute this to higher financing costs for working capital, project loans, and compliance with safety standards.

The LPG Operators Association of Bangladesh stated that while they respect BERC-announced prices, they cannot always comply as rates are not adjusted quickly enough to reflect changing market conditions.

M Shamsul Alam, energy adviser to the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB), alleged that some LPG companies are creating an artificial shortage through stockpiling. He called for a judicial investigation into profiteering and punishment for those involved.
